description.narrative: Insatsen var initialt ett stöd till FN:s nya landprogram för Kenya, Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (SDCF), 2022-2026, som kanaliseras genom en Multi Partner Trust Fund för ändamålet. Det svenska stödet ska främst användas för kapacitetsstärkning av MPTF:s management i Nairobi, inklusive sekretariatet för SDG Partnership Platform, båda inhysta under UN Resident Coordinator's Office (UNRCO). Kapacitetsstärkningen riktar sig främst mot områdena ungdomar och sysselsättning; katastrofriskreduceringe och resiliens; miljö, klimat och grön finansiering samt hanteringen av SDGPP. Ytterligare bidrag har därefter givits till fonden för att stödja särskilda ändamål genom sk Joint Programs.

The contribution was initially a support to the UN:s new country program for Kenya - the Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (SDCF), 2022-2026, which is channeled through the Multi Partner Trust Fund set up for this purpose. The Swedish support will primarily be used for capacity strengthening of the MPTF's management in Nairobi, including the Secretariat for the SDG Partnership Platform, both hosted within the UN Resident Coordinator's Office (UNRCO). The capacity strengthening is focused on the areas of youth and employment; disaster risk reduction and resilience; environment, climate and green financing; and SDGPP management. Additional contributions to the Fund have thereafter been provided for special purposes through so called Joint Programs.

The main objectives of the intervention are:
- improved coordination of the UNCT, together with GoK, donors and other stakeholders, for a more effective and efficient implementation of the UNSDCF in alignment with Kenya's development plans;
- contribute to enhanced resource mobilization through the SDGPP and development of innovative finance solutions for investments in prioritised sectors (and sub-sectors) as identfied by Kenya and in the SDCF.
The SDG MPTF Kenya was established in July 2022, with the purpose to support the delivery of UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2022 2026, enhance the UN to deliver as one through Joint Programs and to support the country in achieving the SDGs. The Fund builds on the existing Partnerships Platform (SDGPP) that was established in 2017 to support the UNDAF 20182022. Sida's first contribution is loosely earmarked to the Fund's "Enabler Window", and more specifically for Strengthening the Capacity of the SDG MPTF Kenya Secretariat (the Secretariat) by financing four positions at the RCO and SDGPP, as well as a smaller budget for "emerging, strategic issues". A second contribution to the Fund was agreed upon in a first amendment to the MPTF SAA and disbursed in late December 2022, earmarked for a Joint Program on drought response and resilience under the Window for Strategic Pillar 2, "Planet and Prosperity". A third contribution to the Fund was agreed upon in a second amendment to the MPTF SAA and disbursed in late December 2023, earmarked for a bridge Joint Program on Social and Child Protection under the Window for Strategic Pillar 1, "People and Peace". The objectives of the intervention have, thus, been updated with regards to the additional funding to the MPTF by these amendments.
The main objectives of the intervention are: - improved coordination of the UNCT, together with GoK, donors and other stakeholders, for a more effective and efficient implementation of the UNSDCF in alignment with Kenya's development plans; - contribute to enhanced resource mobilization through the SDGPP and development of innovative finance solutions for investments in prioritized sectors (and sub-sectors) as identified by Kenya and in the SDCF.
For amendment I: The main purpose and overall objective is to enhance response and recovery for communities affected by drought in Northern Kenya while enhancing long term climate resilience response and recovery targeting 75,000 people and 200,000 livestock. The specific objectives are: - to provide improved access to safe water and hygiene for 75,000 drought affected vulnerable people and 200,000 livestock in Turkana, Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, and Marsabit counties by ensuring continued availability and access to essential services and strengthened climate smart food production for 1,000 households impacted by the drought in Garissa, Turkana and Tana River counties.
For amendment II: The expected results are: - To enhance the capacity and opportunities for the poor and vulnerable to improve and sustain their livelihoods and welfare; - To facilitate and follow up successful achievement of government's commitment to expand social protection coverage including cost sharing whenever possible; - Social and child protection systems have enhanced technical and financial capacity to develop and manage programs at scale; - Functional coordination at the national and county levels for inter-sectoral linkages is enhanced; - Government and partners have financial and technical capacity to review, develop and implement policies, legislation and strategies delivering on the right to social protection and child protection-
For amendment III: The expected results for the Joint Program are: - To support coordination, data management and evidence based policymaking, planning and budgeting for enhanced child protection and social protection outcomes - Enhanced systems and capacity of the national and county governments, non-state institutions and communities to efficiently deliver well-coordinated, inclusive, accessible, equitable and resilient/shock-responsive social and child protection services to Kenyans, addressing multiple dimensions of poverty and vulnerability across the life cycle. -Enhanced capacity of national and county governments, non state institutions and communities to strengthen and expand inclusive and sustainable child protection and social protection programmes and systems For this Joint Program Swedish contribution to the MPTF, the interventions objectives are hereby updated with regards to the funding for Social and Child Protection

description.narrative:
The Fund reports annually by end-May on Fund Status and Progress as per the previous calendar year. Examples of results and achievements reported include:
Direct cost Enabler window
Youth empowerment advisory capacity
- 1.6 million youth reached through digital and deliberative platforms and community-based channels that strengthened civic participation, close to 48 per cent of whom are young women.
Disaster Risk and Resilience advisory Capacity
- USD 5 million in Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) Anticipatory Action funding mobilised, establishing pre-arranged financing for drought response.
- 476,000 hectares of land restored through DRR and resilience interventions in 2025.
People and Peace Thematic Window
Under the People and Peace Window, the Fund strengthened inclusive governance, peacebuilding and social protection systems through policy reforms, improved service delivery and stronger community resilience.
Integrating Peacebuilding and Social Cohesion in Refugee Management in Kenya
- 84.8% reduction in conflict incidents in Dadaab between June and December 2025, following community dialogue and peacebuilding interventions.
Joint Programme on Social Protection and Child Protection
- In 2025, the JP, implemented by FAO, ILO, UNICEF and WFP, made major gains in strengthening Kenya's child protection and social protection systems and hence contributing largely to systems change.
- A key milestone was the approval of the Kenya Social Protection Act 2025, which established a rights-based framework for expanded and better-coordinated social assistance.
- Design and approval of the USD 127 million Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project (KSEIP II), shaping core components on nutrition (NICHE), adolescent support and climate-resilient economic inclusion.
- Delivery systems, including the Enhanced Single Registry, CCTP-MIS and CD-MIS, were upgraded to improve targeting, data integration and payment efficiency.
- The JP advanced inclusion of informal and rural workers by supporting county action plans in Kisumu, Mombasa and Busia, and by organising Social Protection Fairs that reached 5,000 workers and enabled 531 new registrations with SHA and NSSF.
- Over 168,000 children affected by violence accessed health, justice and social services, including nearly 50,000 through case management. Parenting programmes reached 5,185 caregivers and community sensitisation engaged 82,000 people. National progress included finalising six regulations under the Children Act 2022 and securing a 400 per cent budget increase for emergency and refugee services.
Planet and Prosperity Thematic Window
The Planet and Prosperity Window advanced climate-resilient development and green economic transformation through integrated value chain approaches, nature-based solutions and innovative financing models.
The Joint Programme on Sustainable Integrated Water Management
- The JP delivers climate-resilient water solutions across Kenya's ASAL counties of Garissa, Wajir, Marsabit and Mandera. The programme prioritises sand dams as a core solution, providing reliable, year-round water access by recharging aquifers and reducing evaporation losses, benefitting households, livestock and smallholder production.
Strategic Enabler of Partnerships Window
The Strategic Enabler of Partnerships Window deepened collaboration between government, private sector and development partners, mobilising investments.
The Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Development Impact Bond (ASRH-DIB), through the SDG PP
- 754,083 girls aged 15 to 19 reached across 10 counties with family planning services, cumulatively from 2023 to 2025.
* Financially, the Fund's balance by end 2025 was 19% and its expenditure rate 61%, which is an improvement from last year and may constitute proof of increased effectiveness.
Examples of results contributing to desirable behavior change among actors:
- In 2025, the Fund demonstrated its catalytic value by unlocking additional financing, strengthening government systems, advancing innovative financing models and deepening partnerships across public, private and civil society actors. It also demonstrated ambition to only support initiatives that have potential for scale and impact.
- The JP on Social and Child Protection drove major system-level reforms and expanded equitable access to child and social protection services nationwide. The systems strengthening has resulted in 1.7 million households being reached through the Inua Jamii social cash transfer programme, the first major expansion in over a decade.
- The JP on Sustainable Integrated Water Management is assessed as having great potential for results at scale. It involves more than ten UN entities joining forces with national and devolved government and the private sector. Its progress so far reflects successful climate finance mobilisation, strengthened institutional coordination and readiness for delivery at scale. Swedens provision of an unearmarked grant of USD 1.2 million under the pooled SDG Multi-Partner Trust Fund Kenya, UN Kenya was able to unlock an additional USD 20 million from the Climate Adaptation Fund for the benefit of water access for more than a million additional Kenyans.
- A defining feature is the ownership model: communities lead construction and management of sand dams through local committees, while counties integrate the infrastructure into planning and budgets, ensuring sustainability and maintenance of investments beyond project cycles.
- The programme is also unlocking private sector participation through an Adopt-a-Sand Dam model, enabling companies to co-invest in scaling infrastructure while maintaining community and government ownership. Implementation is underway in Garissa and Marsabit, with expansion planned for Wajir and Mandera.
The Strategic Enabler of Partnerships Window, including the SDG Partnership Platform (SDGPP) deepened collaboration between government, private sector and development partners, mobilizing investments.
- Here, the Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Development Impact Bond (ASRH DIB) is an example of the Fund's support for innovative approaches to development financing and programming. The DIB was developed as a joint UN initiative in Kenya, facilitated by the Fund Secretariat, and has advanced a complementary and catalytic model for adolescent-responsive primary healthcare. The programme demonstrated the viability of outcomes-based financing for ASRH and HIV services across ten counties, introducing accountability mechanisms linking service delivery, real-time data, independent verification and performance-based payments. The DIB combines catalytic grant funding (traditional partners, for example Sweden through unearmarked funding to the MPTF) with private outcome investment (philanthropies, private sector) and independent verification mechanisms. The catalytic approach has moreover helped to unlock additional pooled financing from the global Joint SDG Fund.
- From a private-sector perspective, the DIB has demonstrated that adolescent health can be structured as a credible outcomes-based investment opportunity, rather than only a grant-funded social intervention, as it helped create market confidence and a structured pipeline for future participation by private and philanthropic actors.
